plain_english: The contract starts on 1 June 2025, lasts for one year, and will keep renewing every six months unless you, the freelancer, send a written notice at least 60 days before the current term ends to stop it.
what_it_means_for_you: You’ll stay bound by the agreement for another six months unless you remember to give a 60‑day written notice before the end of each term.
risk_reasons: The contract will keep renewing automatically, which could extend your obligations beyond what you expect.
You must give written notice at least 60 days before the term ends, so missing the deadline could lock you in for another six months.
questions_to_ask: What form and address should the written notice of non‑renewal take?
Can I give notice by email or only by postal mail?
What happens if I miss the 60‑day notice—does the contract simply renew or are there penalties?
Will the compensation terms change on each renewal?
Is there any way to terminate earlier than the renewal date without penalty?
evidence_quote: The Agreement shall automatically renew for successive 6-month periods unless the Freelancer provides written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days before expiry.
